deep.reconstruction:
Context: Riemann is evaluating the elliptic modulus functions k, k' and the complete integral K at the boundary |q|=1 of the unit disc, q = e^{ix}, for rational x/pi (the 'Grenzfaelle' of the elliptic modular functions, cusps and nearby limit values). The previous page did log k; this page treats -log k' and log(2K/pi). Heading line: -log k' = 8 sum_t (1/t) q^t/(1-q^{2t}) = 4i sum_t 1/(t sin(t x)) (the image reads 't sin tx'; the machine transcription 't+itx' is wrong). The step is q^t/(1-q^{2t}) = 1/(q^{-t}-q^t) = i/(2 sin tx). Similarly log(2K/pi) = 4 sum q^t/(t(1+q^t)) = log((q0+q)/(q0-q)) + 2i sum (1/t) tan(t x/2), where q0 is apparently the value of q at the pole/reference point (q0 = e^{i pi/2}-type constant, not fully clear from the scan) and the log((q0+q)/(q0-q)) term absorbs the slowly convergent part.

Method (common to all cases, modern restatement): for x = rational multiple of pi, write t = N t' + s with N the period of the summand in t, so the series becomes sum_{t'>=0} sum_{s=1}^{N-1} f(s)/(N t'+s). Use 1/(Nt'+s) = integral_0^1 u^{N t'+s-1} du, sum the geometric series in t' to get integral_0^1 sum_s f(s) u^{s-1}/(1-u^N) du. Then expand f(s), a function of alpha^{ms} with alpha an N-th root of unity, as a finite Fourier series in s: for omega^N=1, omega != 1, 1/(1-omega) = -(1/N) sum_{sigma=0}^{N-1} sigma omega^sigma (Riemann writes this via the generating identity 1/(1-r omega) = sum_{sigma<N} r^sigma omega^sigma/(1-r^N) and differentiating or specialising r). Partial fractions u^{s-1}/(1-u^N) = (1/N) sum_t alpha^{t s}... alpha^t/(1-alpha^t u) alpha^{-ts} turn the s-sum into coefficients c(t) = sum_s sum_sigma (...) alpha^{s(...)-ts}; this is a character sum that is nonzero only for t in a few residue classes (e.g. t = m(2r+1) mod 4n), and integral_0^1 alpha^t du/(1-alpha^t u) = -log(1-alpha^t). So -log k' becomes a finite sum of log(1-alpha^j) with explicit rational weights.

Case 1) x = m pi/(2n), m odd: -log k' = 4i sum_{t'} sum_{s=1}^{4n-1} 1/((4nt'+s) sin(s m pi/(2n))) = 8 int_0^1 sum_s u^{s-1}/(1-u^{4n}) alpha^{ms}/(1-alpha^{2ms}) du with alpha = e^{2 pi i/(4n)} (using 1/sin = 2i alpha^{ms}.../(...) up to sign). Then 1/(1-alpha^{2ms}) = -(1/2n) sum_{sigma=0}^{2n-1} sigma alpha^{2ms sigma}, giving a double sum with exponent alpha^{ms(2 sigma+1)} alpha^{-ts}; summing over s picks t = m(2r+1) mod 4n. Result stated: 8 sum_r log(1-alpha^{m(2r+1)}) (1/4n)(1/2n)(...) ... [the intermediate coefficient is elided with dots on the page], finally = pi i((m-2)n - 4 sum_{s=0}^{n-1} E(m(2s+1)/(4n))), E = floor (Riemann's E = integer part). The step from log(1-e^{i theta}) = log(2 sin(theta/2)) + i(theta-pi)/2 (0<theta<2pi) is what produces floor functions: the real parts cancel by symmetry r -> -r-1 and only the imaginary part, a sawtooth in theta, survives.

Case 2) x = m pi/n, n odd: an extra term -(q+q0)/(q-q0) (pi^2/(4n^2)) q0^{-n} appears (a pole contribution: the s with sin=0, i.e. the term that cannot be handled by the finite-sum identity), then the same procedure with alpha = e^{2 pi i/(2n)}, kernel coefficient ((sigma-(n-1)/2)/n) which is the sawtooth ((y)) = absolute least residue/sawtooth function (the previous page defines (x) = absolut kleinster Rest), NOT a Legendre symbol. Two residue classes of t (t = m(2r+1) mod 2n and t = m(2r+1)+n) are separated; the two log sums combine to log of ratios alpha^{...}, then are reduced to sums over s=1..(n-1)/2 of ((s/n)) times differences of log(1-alpha^{2ms+...}). Introducing mu with m mu = 1 mod n, reindexing gives 4 pi i (-1)^{m+1} sum_{s=1}^{(n-1)/2} ((mu s/n)), and the final line: (-1)^{m+1}( (pi^2/(4n^2)) (q+q0)/(q-q0) + pi i( ((n-1)/n) mu - 4 sum_{s=1}^{(n-1)/2} E(mu s/n + 1/2) ) ). Several intermediate lines (the one with '(...)' and the line beginning '= A + 4 pi i sum (s/n)(...)') are partly illegible or abbreviated.

log(2K/pi), cases 1-3 (this page bottom and next page): K/(pi/2) = theta_3^2 with the series 4 sum q^t/(t(1+q^t)) understood as log of a theta-quotient expansion; it is rewritten with tan(t x/2). Case 1) x = 2 m pi/n, n odd, alpha = e^{pi i/(2n)} [crossed-out '-pi-']: finite sum identity 1/(1+r omega) = sum_{sigma<n} (-1)^sigma r^sigma omega^sigma/(1+r^n); leads, on the next page, to log(2K/pi) = log((q0+q)/(q0-q)) + 2 pi i sum_{s=1}^{(n-1)/2} (( 2ms/n + 1/2 )-( 2ms/n )) (sawtooth differences, each equal to 1/2 times a sign-type quantity). Case 2) x = m pi/n with n even (page says 'gerade', transcription '[?]'), m odd, alpha = e^{2 pi i/(4n)}: A + 2 pi i sum_{nu=1}^{n-1} (-1)^nu ((mu nu - n)/(2n)), m mu = 1 mod 2n. Case 3) x = m pi/(2n): A + 2 pi i sum (-1)^nu ((mu nu - 2n)/(4n)), m mu = 1 mod 4n. Here A collects the explicit pole term (pi^2/(4n^2))(q+q0)/(q-q0).

Problem served: obtain closed-form (algebraic-trigonometric, Dedekind-sum-like) values or exact asymptotic/limit behaviour of log k, log k', log 2K/pi when the argument approaches a rational point of the boundary; i.e. determine the phase (an imaginary part given by a sum of floor functions) and the singular real part (pole of order given by 1/(q - q0)-type term) at each cusp. This is the content of the posthumously published fragment on limiting cases of elliptic modular functions.
errors: Heading line: transcription '4i sum 1/(t+itx)' is a misreading; the image gives 1/(t sin tx), which is the correct simplification of 8 q^t/(t(1-q^{2t})) = 4i/(t sin tx). As typed by the transcriber the equality is false.

Case 1 (x = m pi/(2n), m odd): the finite sum over s=1..4n-1 contains the term s=2n where sin(s m pi/(2n)) = sin(m pi) = 0, i.e. 1-alpha^{2ms}=0 and the identity 1/(1-omega) = -(1/N) sum sigma omega^sigma is invalid (omega=1). In fact the original series has genuine poles at t = 2n (mod 4n)/gcd structure, so as written the series diverges / the singular terms must be treated separately (as is done explicitly via the A-term in case 2). The page does not show this treatment in case 1 (possibly dropped, possibly the case is meant for m coprime situations where these terms are excluded or interpreted as a regularisation). Flagged as an unjustified step, not certain.

The case-1 intermediate line ends in '...' and the coefficient is not written; the final value pi i((m-2)n - 4 sum E(m(2s+1)/(4n))) cannot be derived from what is on the page alone. I did not verify it.

Notation ambiguity: the bracket ((y)) = y - E(y) - 1/2 type function (absolute least residue 'absolut kleinster Rest', from previous page) is written with parentheses that look like a Legendre symbol (s/n). It is a sawtooth function; reading it as a Legendre symbol would make several steps (e.g. sum over s up to (n-1)/2 with factors ((sigma-(n-1)/2)/n)) meaningless.

Case 2 for -log k': the line labelled '= A + 4 pi i sum (s/n)(...) - 4 sum (s/n)(log(...)-log(...))' rewrites a combination of logs using the real/imag split; the real parts are claimed to cancel and are dropped without comment. Plausible (log|1-e^{i th}| is even in th) but not displayed.

Phrase 'n ungerade' for case 2 of log(2K/pi) on the next page appears as 'n [?] gerade': from the alpha = e^{2 pi i/(4n)} and the mod 2n condition, the case seems to be n any parity with m odd; the parity reading is unclear and I cannot confirm it.

Small slip candidates (unsure): in log(2K/pi) case 1 the stated 'alpha = e^{pi i/(2n)}' vs. the root-of-unity requirement alpha^{2n}... : with 1/(1+r alpha^{2sm}) = sum_{sigma<n} (-1)^sigma r^sigma alpha^{2 s sigma m}/(1+r^n) one needs alpha^{2sm n} = 1 for the identity, which needs alpha a 2n-th root of unity, i.e. e^{2 pi i/(2n)} = e^{pi i/n}; e^{pi i/(2n)} would not satisfy it. The scan digit/first symbol is partly obscured so this may be a transcription issue.

results.what: Closed forms (finite sums of floor/sawtooth functions) for -log k' and log(2K/pi) at rational points x/pi of the boundary |q|=1, with explicit pole term (q+q0)/(q-q0) pi^2/(4n^2) in the odd-denominator cases
results.modern_name: Limit values/radial boundary behaviour of the Jacobi modulus, complementary modulus and K at cusps; Dedekind-sum-type evaluations of log of eta/theta quotients at roots of unity
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind (1877, eta function and Dedekind sums, explicitly drawing on Riemann's fragment); Kronecker limit-type and Hecke/Rademacher evaluations later

results.what: Technique: write sum 1/(Nt+s) f(s) = integral of sum f(s) u^{s-1}/(1-u^N); expand f via sum_sigma sigma omega^sigma / finite Fourier; collapse to finite sums of log(1-alpha^j); read off phase from the sawtooth part of log(1-e^{i theta})
results.modern_name: Evaluation of Dirichlet/Lerch-type series at rational arguments via Gauss-sum / finite Fourier analysis and digamma-type partial fractions (cf. Gauss digamma theorem at rational points)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (digamma at rational arguments, 1812); Kummer/Dirichlet style evaluations; Dedekind and Hurwitz for modular cases

results.what: Finite-sum identity 1/(1-omega) = -(1/N) sum_{sigma=0}^{N-1} sigma omega^sigma for omega^N=1, omega != 1, and its generating version 1/(1-r omega) = sum r^sigma omega^sigma/(1-r^N)
results.modern_name: Finite geometric series / arithmetic of N-th roots of unity

results.modern_name: Principal logarithm of 1-e^{i theta}; Fourier series of the Bernoulli sawtooth

deep.surprise_reason: This is a computational working page that belongs to the material Dedekind published from Riemann's Nachlass as the fragment on limiting cases of the elliptic modular functions, so Riemann's authorship of boundary evaluations at rational points is already known. The page is a systematic case-by-case derivation (denominator odd/even, m odd) with some elided steps; nothing here is plainly beyond what the published fragment contains, though the exact correspondence to the published text was not checked here.
